newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil prices ease with weaker crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil prices ease with weaker crude.

text.p: NWE high sulphur barge prices drifted lower on Wednesday as light short covering provided early support but weaker afternoon crude knocked back early gains.
Low sulphur trade stayed thin and prices weakened with slack demand balancing slightly tighter supplies, traders said.
High sulphur barges were traded several times around $86 a tonne fob ARA in early business, but the market was offered over at this level late in the day with the weaker crude keeping buyers scarce.
Flushing barges traded at $85 a tonne.
Traders said bunker demand was normal around 20kt.
Low sulphur barge trade stayed dull.

The market was pegged steady in early business with buyers and sellers at stand-off, but weaker crude left offers around $2 lower at around $96 fob ARA with best bids notionally pegged around $94 a tonne.
Cargo markets were very quiet. High sulphur prices were around $1 weaker while low sulphur cargoes eased $2.
Crude futures slipped through $19 a barrel to stand around 16 cents lower at $18.95 a barrel at 1700 GMT.
Oversupply kept the physical crude market under pressure. Dated Brent stood around nine cents down at $17.96 a barrel.
